itinerary.heading: Colón, Panama
itinerary.body:
The city of Colón lies by the entrance to the Panama Canal on the Atlantic coast. There are high-quality hotels, hot springs, a thriving handicraft scene and great restaurants with local delicacies.   

Once on board the ship, you’ll pick up your complimentary expedition jacket, explore the ship and attend a mandatory safety drill. After dinner you’ll meet your Expedition Team who will run through some important primers with you. 

Pre-Programme 

If you want to really explore the city or join a Pre-Programme to a beautiful jungle lodge next to the Chagres River, you should arrive a couple of days earlier.

itinerary.heading: Connecting Two Oceans
itinerary.body:
We depart Colón early in the morning to start the process of entering the Panama Canal. The complex canal network is over a hundred years in the making, stretching 80 km through natural and man-made waterways. We’ll wait with anticipation for our allocated slot to enter the first of a series of huge locks. In a feat of modern engineering, these ingenious locks effectively lift the ship more than 26 metres above sea level. If weather allows, the Expedition Team will be out on deck to point out sites of interest around the canal and to talk about the history of this ambitious project.

Roughly half way through the 12-hour transit of the canal, the ship will enter the Gatun Lake section. Created by damning the nearby Chagres River, it is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world. By contrast, the surrounding rainforest is virtually untouched by any development and various flora and fauna native to Central America flourish here undisturbed. Along the shores, you might be lucky enough to spot crocodiles and alligators. Scan the trees for glimpses of monkeys and maybe sloths too.

After a few more locks and lakes, the ship will pass under the Bridge of the Americas and emerge into the Pacific. Passing from one great ocean to another in a day, you’ve just experienced the culmination of centuries of planning, hard work and resourcefulness. It’s sure to be a moment you won’t soon forget.

itinerary.heading: Afro Colombian vibes
itinerary.body:
The little town of Bahía Solano is the largest settlement on Colombia’s Chocó coast, near the mouth of Rio Jella and surrounded by thick jungle. It is also named Ciudad Mutis after the 18th century Spanish botanist, perhaps a reference to the natural biodiversity that exists in the area’s jungles, mangroves, mountains, marshes, rivers, and bays. 

The community here opens their town to us and warmly invite you on a hosted walk through their settlement. Along the way, you’ll meet and talk to the mainly Afro Colombian residents who live alongside indigenous Embera and other Colombians from the interior. Passing by the main church and kindergarten, we’ll come to the local secondary school where students will greet you with a traditional welcome song and show you around their classrooms. Over at the small fishing port, you’ll learn about the town’s fishing co-operative, which is the main source of income for the community. Your tour ends at the seafront where you’ll be treated to a performance of unique Afro Pacific Colombian music and dance. 

There is an optional excursion to the Botanic Gardens located on the long sandy beach of Playa Mecana. The gardens are actually a 170-acre jungle reserve with fascinating nature trails and home to a seed bank plus different reforestation projects. Another potential optional excursion might take you to the fishing village at Playa Huina where you’ll have the opportunity to walk through the jungle to waterfalls with crystal clear swimming holes or to visit a local indigenous community.

itinerary.heading: Relax on board
itinerary.body:
Spend some of your day taking a relaxing walk out on deck, enjoying the seascapes and keeping an eye out for marine wildlife like whales, dolphins and sea birds. If you want to feel closer to the water, go for a dip in the infinity pool or the two outdoor hot tubs, and still be able to admire the scenery.  

This is also a great opportunity to head to the Science Center for lectures with the Expedition Team and to learn more about what you will experience in the following days. Pick one of the proposed Citizen Science programmes to get involved in too, knowing that you will be helping research currently happening around the world. When darkness falls and it’s a starry night, you might also join the Expedition Team out on deck to do some stargazing. Or settle into a comfortable seat in the Explorer Lounge & Bar to raise a glass or two with new-found friends.

itinerary.heading: Made in Montecristi
itinerary.body:
We cross the Equator early in the morning. You can join a traditional ceremony on board where we seek King Neptune’s blessing. If we are lucky, he may even make an appearance before we reach our first call in Ecuador.  

Our main tour of the day will be to the handicraft town of Montecristi located 8km inland from the tuna-fishing port city of Manta. It was established in the 16th century by manteños fleeing the frequent pirate raids on the coast. Montecristi, Ecuador is the actual birthplace of traditional Panama hats, despite the name. The misnomer originates from when President Roosevelt wore one of these hats on a visit to the Panama Canal in 1904, sparking their popularity worldwide. You’ll see many shops throughout the town selling the genuine article in all sizes and shades, expertly handwoven from the leaves of the jipijapa tree by local artisans. 

Aside from hat-hunting, you can spend time browsing the stalls at the pretty plaza, admiring the architecture of the church, or looking at the varied street art. One prominent mural at the plaza depicts General Eloy Alfaro, two-time Ecuadorian President and Montecristi native. You might also have time to head to the top of the main hill where there is a museum and grandiose mausoleum in honour of Alfaro who was also known as the Viejo Luchador or "Old Warrior".

itinerary.heading: Ecuador’s other Galápagos
itinerary.body:
Isla de la Plata is a part of Parque National Machalilla, Ecuador’s only coastal national park. The island sits quite far off the coast and is prone to large waves that can make landings a challenge. Its name as the ‘Island of Silver’ is thought to come from the belief that English seaman Francis Drake buried a bunch of silver treasure here. Or it’s possibly because all the bird guano reflected in the sunshine gave the island a shiny, silvery look when seen from the mainland. No treasure has ever been found on the island though which only measures less than 6 square kilometres.

Still, whatever the island lacks in size or silver, it more than makes up for in a range of wildlife that rivals that of the Galápagos Islands. If we are able to go ashore here successfully, keen bird watchers among you will enjoy walking on the island with binoculars at the ready to spot some of the 32 species of bird found here, like famous blue-footed boobies, nesting waved albatrosses, pelicans, gannets, and frigate birds. The waters around the island are equally diverse and you might be lucky enough to see whales, manta rays, green turtles, and dolphins.

itinerary.heading: Growing green gold
itinerary.body:
Machala’s main claim to fame is Puerto Bolivar, an important Ecuadorian port for the export of coffee, cocoa, shrimp and bountiful bananas which the locals call oro verde – ‘green gold’. ￼As part of a choice of optional excursions, you can visit a local banana plantation and also try and spot hummingbirds, parakeets and howler monkeys in Buenaventura Nature Reserve to the south. Puyango Petrified Forest is nearby with one of the largest collections of fossilised trees in the world, thought to be about 100 million years-old, as old as the Andes Mountains themselves.

At Puerto Bolivar, you can feast on fresh seafood at one of the many harbour restaurants and enjoy views of the natural mangrove swamps of Isla Jambeli opposite. Machala itself has all the charm you’d expect from a small coastal city, including friendly locals, cute plazas and unusual monuments dedicated to sort-fish and bananeros. The restaurants are evolving and beginning to dabble in the hip modern cuisine which Ecuador and Peru are increasingly known for.

itinerary.heading: At your leisure
itinerary.body: Enjoy another day at your leisure aboard the ship. Take advantage of the many onboard facilities or join in on lectures, perhaps on Peruvian culture and history, as we prepare you for what’s still to come. Spend some time up on deck sun-bathing, slip into your bathing suit and lie back into the bubbles of one of the outdoor hot tubs or bask in a state of zen during a guided meditation class. And if the warm weather hasn’t opened up your pores, a session in the sauna is bound to do the trick. When you’ve had enough of the sun for the day, head back inside to join an art workshop, or maybe recap your voyage so far with your fellow guests in the Explorer Lounge & Bar.

itinerary.heading: Ancient Kingdoms
itinerary.body:
Buffeted by the wind and waves of the Pacific, Salaverry can be a hard port to access. If all goes to plan though, it will be a good transit point to explore Trujillo, Peru’s third largest city, as well as an array of archaeological sites scattered throughout the surrounding region. 

Trujillo sits in a fertile valley oasis irrigated by the Moche River. It boasts a colourful baroque 17th century cathedral, 10 colonial churches, and many neoclassical mansions, not to mention one of the longest mosaic murals in the world at the local university. However, it is more than likely that your focus will be elsewhere and on things not so modern. 

The city of Chan Chan was raised by the Chimu Empire which appeared in the region around 900 AD. The vast ruins of the 20-square kilometre complex include the Tschudi temple-citadel and Huaca Esmeralda. On the other side of Trujillo are the Mochican pyramids of the Sun and the Moon which pre-date Chan Chan by a few hundred years. Huaca del Sol in particular is the largest adobe structure on the continent while Huaca del Luna is more detailed with many of its pastel frescos still visible.

itinerary.heading: On a high
itinerary.body:
We dock in Callao and travel a short distance to Lima airport for your flight to Quito, the capital of Ecuador. After you arrive and the transfer brings you to your hotel, you’ll have the rest of the day to explore at your leisure, with dinner served at the hotel. 

Originally settled by the Quitu tribe in the first millennium, Quito was eventually integrated into the Inca Empire before being refounded in 1534 by Spanish conqueror Sebastian de Benalcásar. Take a walk in the city’s historic centre to see splendidly restored period buildings and colonial-era churches lining the narrow, cobbled streets. You’ll understand why Quito’s historic centre is described as the largest, least-altered, and best-preserved historic areas in the Americas. For those reasons, it was among the first places to ever be declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1978. 

Don’t be surprised if you should feel a little short of breath when exploring the city though. At 2,850 metres above sea level, Quito is the second highest capital in the world after La Paz in Bolivia which is about 650 metres higher.

itinerary.heading: Views from the Middle of the World
itinerary.body:
Once you have enjoyed your breakfast, we´ll take you to the charming colonial quarter and enjoy a sightseeing tour of the area. Starting with Plaza San Francisco, we´ll visit the  Church choir and patios of the Franciscan order. We´ll then stroll through the handsome streets to the Jesuit church of La Compañía with its stunning gold-leaf interior 

A trip to Ecuador wouldn't be complete without a photo depicting one foot in the northern hemisphere and another in the southern hemisphere. Continue by coach to the Middle of the World City, located just 8.3 mi (13.5 km) north of Quito, that stands to honor the Geodesic Mission that established latitude 0 in the 18th century. Depending on the time available, you´ll be able to visit the surroundings of the small village. You will also have the opportunity to visit the the Intiñan Museum, offering an ecological and scientific discovery space that transports visitors back to ancient times, allowing them to learn about the worldview, customs and traditions of ancient cultures. 

Lunch is served at El Crater restaurant which overlooks Pululahua Volcano.  

In the afternoon you´ll return to your hotel in Quito.  

Dinner will be served at the hotel and the evening is spent at your leisure.

itinerary.heading: Arriving at Santa Cruz Island
itinerary.body:
You’ll start your day with breakfast at the hotel before we drive to Quito Airport for the flight to the Galápagos Islands (via Guayaquil).  When we arrive at Baltra’s airport, our local representative will transfer you to Itabaca Channel where a small ferry brings you to the island of Santa Cruz.  

We’ll travel through a rural agricultural area surrounded by wild landscapes and many different species of flora and fauna. If you are lucky, you might spot a few of the famous finches which inspired Darwin’s theory of evolution. The highlands are one of the best places on the island to observe giant tortoises in their natural habitat. Easy to spot, they lumber around eating grass and leaves and wallow in the small, muddy rain-formed pools. Younger ones tend to be smaller with shinier carapaces while the larger, older ones wear weathered and worn shells like the distinguished armour of a long life – over 100 years in the wild.  

Enjoy lunch in the Highlands. 

Once you’ve settled into your hotel in the town of Puerto Ayora, we’ll walk to the nearby Charles Darwin Research Station. The station hosts educational museums on both the history and development of the Galápagos Islands and the range of protections given to this natural heritage. Native giant land tortoises can also be observed here, and the station is the only place in the Galápagos where most of the different species reside at one site.   

The afternoon is at your leisure to explore the small, picturesque Puerto Ayora and its many local arts and crafts shops. See the colourful murals at the churches around town or take a short walk to Tortuga Bay to look for marine iguanas, crabs, and white tip reef sharks among the mangroves. Dinner will be served at the hotel´s restaurant.

itinerary.heading: Galápagos Island Hopping
itinerary.body:
After breakfast, we'll begin to explore the islands that have become synonymous with the theory of evolution and hailed as a natural laboratory for natural selection. The range of wildlife on display in the islands is mind-boggling, full of endemic species and subspecies from the wonderful to the weird and everything in between. Over two days, you’ll visit two islands out of a possible six, going to one island each day by boat. Which ones you’ll see will be on the say-so of the park authorities who regulate and assign visitors a month beforehand.

Will it be Bartolomé Island, famous for the dramatic Pinnacle Rock and the rare colony of Galápagos penguins at its base? Or perhaps, it’ll be North Seymour Island, site of large populations of the hilarious blue-footed boobies, swallow-tailed gulls and magnificent frigatebirds? Santa Fe Island is known to have some of the most beautiful coves in the archipelago with beaches covered in lounging sea lions. Or maybe you’ll go to South Plaza Island where a growing colony of land iguanas roam among the prickly pear cactus trees.

It’s clear that whichever two islands you get to set foot on and explore, you’re in for a real treat! You’ll go on walks ashore and learn about the island’s geology, human history, and the exceptionally diverse wildlife all around you. After two days, you’ll understand just why Darwin was so impressed by the islands and why they inspired his world-changing theory.

itinerary.heading: Return to mainland Ecuador
itinerary.body:
After breakfast at the hotel, it’ll be time to make our way to Baltra airport to fly to Guayaquil and from there on to your connecting flight home. 

With that, your expedition is over. You’ll have journeyed from the marvel of human engineering at the Panama Canal and its complex lock system through to the Galápagos Islands, birthplace of Darwin’s radical biological theory of natural selection and a sanctuary for unique wildlife found nowhere else in the world.

itinerary.heading: Las Palmas Welcome
itinerary.body:
Your adventure begins in Las Palmas – a continent in miniature

Welcome to Gran Canaria, third largest of the Canary islands and a place that has seen pirates, privateers and even Christopher Columbus come and go.

In the capital Las Palmas, head to Vegueta the city’s Old Town district and stroll through its narrow cobbled streets and alleyways. Visit the Cathedral of Santa Ana and its bell tower for panoramic views. Or why not book a Pre-Programme and take in the islands geological and volcanic wonders including Bandama Crater?

Once aboard MS Spitsbergen, collect your complimentary expedition jacket and settle into your cabin. Your adventure has begun.

itinerary.heading: Bound for Madeira
itinerary.body:
Soak up the sun during a relaxing day at sea

As we sail towards Madeira, shake off any stress and strain you came with and prepare to get into explorer mode.

This is your day to do what you like. Soak yourself in the hot tubs or work up a sweat in the gym, take in an Expedition Team lecture on Madeira’s history and wildlife, or simply relax in a comfortable chair and watch the sea pass by.  

This is also a great time to get to know your crew and fellow explorers. Why not strike up a conversation at the bar and see what you have in common with your fellow shipmates. We're sure you'll have lots to talk about.

itinerary.heading: Verdant Madeira
itinerary.body:
A lush island rising from the sea

Our day in Madeira begins with an included tour, where we'll explore the quaint capital Funchal, before sampling the island's famed fortified wines.

See the beautiful wooden ceiling of Funchal Cathedral, head to the farmers' market to try the ananas-banana – or pineapple banana – which only grows here, and take the cable car to the picturesque village of Monte for glorious views.

For something different, why not slide your way back down to Funchal in carros de cesto, wicker baskets with seats set on wooden skis. Or join an optional excursion to see the island’s charming hamlets, set among terraced fields.

itinerary.heading: Unspoilt Porto Santo
itinerary.body:
Picturesque scenery, rolling hills and undisturbed sandy beaches

The approach to Porto Santo is renowned for its dolphins and seabirds. Keep an eye out for Sandwich Terns, Manx Shearwaters and Bulwer’s Petrels swooping down from above.

We dock at Vila Baleira. Be sure to take in the charming Nossa Senhora da Piedade church and the house Christopher Columbus lived in. Then relax with a glass of locally-made vinho do Porto Santo before exploring the island's miles of golden sandy beaches.

For gorgeous views, take an optional excursion to Ilhéu da Cal, or to the summits of Pico do Castelo and Pico Branco. You'll be rewarded with some truly stunning vistas.

itinerary.heading: Return to the Canaries
itinerary.body:
Enjoy a relaxing day at sea as your adventure continues

After your days of exploration on land, you’ll most likely be ready for a leisurely day aboard the ship.

Recline in the panoramic Explorer Lounge, drink in hand, and take in the view. Watch the waters for whales and dolphins, reflect on your adventures so far, edit your photos, update your travel journal, or simply rest your legs.

Why not spend some time in the library reading up on the places you’ll visit, or attend lectures from the Expedition Team on the next stage of your Canary Islands adventure? Whatever you decide, the volcanic island of Lanzarote awaits.

itinerary.heading: Fire Island of Lanzarote
itinerary.body:
Natural wonders, spectacular volcanic landscapes – this is Lanzarote

Just 78 miles off the African coast, Lanzarote’s spartan, desert-like landscape and eroded volcanic formations are a geologist’s dream.

Once a popular fishing port, Arrecife is now a charming, sun-kissed town. Explore the Old Town's whitewashed fisherman houses, 17th century church San Ginés and 18th century Casa de los Arroyo.

Lanzarote’s stunning beaches are breathtaking. Head to white-sand El Reducto beach, protected by natural reefs. Or join an optional excursion to discover Timanfaya National Park or famous Jameos del Agua lagoons and long lava tubes.

itinerary.heading: Capital of the Canaries
itinerary.body:
Explore Tenerife's history, national parks and volcanoes

We dock at Santa Cruz, the joint-capital of the Canary Islands with its vibrant harbour and old-world yet modern feel.

Walk uphill to the Plaza de la Candelaria and take in the facades of the old Casino and 18th century Palacio Carta. Explore the beautiful plazas of Príncipe de Asturias and Los Patos then the stunning García Sanabria Park filled with tropical flowers, ferns and hidden sculptures.

Join one of our optional excursions to the world’s third-largest volcano. Its unique landscape of craters, volcanic cones, ancient rocks and streams of petrified lava is truly unforgettable.

itinerary.location: Santa Cruz de la Palma, Spain
itinerary.heading: Las Palma: La Isla Bonita
itinerary.body:
Discover one of the Canary Islands most attractive towns – Santa Cruz

Known as La Isla Bonita or ‘The Pretty Island’, Las Palma is home to unspoiled pine and laurel forests, banana trees and palm groves.

After arriving in Santa Cruz, head to the vibrant main street lined with magnificent Renaissance-era buildings with lavishly adorned plants and flowers. For many, it’s the best example of Canarian architecture. Then explore the eccentric La Palma Island Museum set inside an old convent.

Hiking in La Palma is superb. Join us on an optional excursion to the volcanoes and spectacular Caldera de Taburiente National Park with walks among the best in the archipelago.

itinerary.heading: The charms of El Hierro
itinerary.body:
Traditional El Hierro, a beautiful gem and UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve

The youngest, smallest and most remote Canary Island, El Hierro is a volcanic island hewn by eruptions, powerful winds and landslides. It's unique geology is formed from an oceanic volcano, and it's no wonder that UNESCO has classified it as a World Biosphere Reserve.

With no natural harbours, we dock at La Estaca then head for Valverde, an easy-going, traditional small town without traffic lights or fancy shops.

Walking is the best way to explore El Hierro. Discover shimmering natural pools, lava-sculpted rocks, pine forests, peaceful flower meadows and twisted trees, on an optional excursion.

itinerary.location: San Sebastián de la Gomera, Spain
itinerary.heading: Untamed La Gomera
itinerary.body:
Experience an authentic slice of Canarian life, La Gomera

La Gomera is not just the second smallest of the Canary Islands, it’s also the most untamed.

Head into the Old Town at San Sebastian and take in the Iglesia de la Virgen de la Asuncion, where Columbus and his men are said to have prayed before setting sail. Then visit the intriguing Archaeological Museum of La Gomera to learn all about the island’s first settlers. 

The islanders developed a loud whistling called el silbo to communicate over long distances. Experience this or the jaw-dropping Garajonay National Park, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, on an optional excursion.

itinerary.location: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
itinerary.heading: Back to Gran Canaria
itinerary.body:
A return visit to the most diverse of Canary Islands

Your expedition ends where it started, exploring Gran Canaria's diverse dunes, subtropical valleys and picturesque pine forests.

With 60 miles of beach and almost 620 miles of marked trails, Gran Canaria's natural features are made for walkers. Why not get onto the trail network, and have this UNESCO Biosphere Reserve to yourself?

Alternatively, learn about the Guanches, the original inhabitants of the archipelago at the Museo Canario. Or extend your stay with our optional Post-Programme. Whatever’s next, we look forward to welcoming you back on your next adventure soon.

itinerary.heading: Explore vibrant Quito
itinerary.body:
Begin your adventure in this historic equatorial city

Your expedition starts in Quito, high up in the foothills of the Ecuadorian Andes. Straddling the Equator, it feels like springtime year-round. Beneath Quito's bustling, modern façade lie its ancient Incan roots.

Quito's UNESCO-listed Old Town, the largest and best-preserved historical centre in the Americas, blends Spanish colonial architecture with Moorish and indigenous influences. Settle into your hotel, then head out to explore.

If you have time, join our four-day Pre-Programme to discover the lost civilisation of the Incas, including the breathtaking mountain stronghold of Machu Picchu.

itinerary.heading: Climb Cotopaxi Volcano
itinerary.body:
Visit one of Ecuador's natural wonders

Your first stop is the bustling Sangolqui open-air market, where you can sample Andean specialities and buy handicrafts from friendly stallholders.

Spot wild llamas, Andean Gulls, and maybe the majestic condor on your drive through Andean moorlands to Cotopaxi National Park. We’ll take a walk to the beautiful Limpiopungo Lagoon.

The day's main highlight is Cotopaxi Volcano. You'll walk to a height of almost 12,800 ft up this stunning active volcano. Almost perfectly conical, it features one of the world's only equatorial glaciers. For lunch, you'll enjoy some fantastic regional cooking before returning to the hotel.

itinerary.heading: Your cruise begins
itinerary.body:
Get ready to explore spectacular Galápagos

This morning we'll fly to Baltra Island, where you'll board MS Santa Cruz II, meet your Expedition Team, and settle in for your Galápagos Islands cruise. From the airport to your ship and tour, every effort is made to protect the delicate environment.

You'll get your first glimpse of the islands' incredible diversity on Mosquera Islet, home to one of the largest sea lion colonies in the archipelago. We'll take small expedition boats ashore to get a closer look.

As you stroll across flat and sandy dunes, look out for Blue-footed Boobies and Sally Lightfoot crabs. And learn about the marine and terrestrial ecosystems from your guides.

itinerary.heading: San Cristobal's tortoises
itinerary.body:
Meet the Galápagos' giant tortoises

Your first stop today is the Cerro Colorado Tortoise Reserve – a breeding centre for the highly endangered giant tortoise. It's also home to other endemic species, including the San Cristobal Mockingbird and lava lizard.

The giant tortoise is probably the most iconic of all Galápagos wildlife, with a lifespan of over 100 years. Here, they thrive, ambling around forests similar to their natural habitat.

Our small expedition boats will then take you to Punta Pitt, the only site in the Galápagos where you might see three species of boobies. Enjoy a nature walk, explore the coastline by boat, or snorkel and swim in the crystal-clear water.

itinerary.location: Santa Fe Island & South Plaza Island
itinerary.heading: Santa Fe and South Plaza
itinerary.body:
Spot wildlife against idyllic backdrops

We start the day with a scenic nature walk on the blissful beaches of Santa Fe, home to the endemic Barrington land iguana and a colony of sea lions.

You can go swimming or snorkelling from our expedition boats, take our kayaks for a paddle around the island, or join a trip in our glass-bottomed boat and observe the marine life below. After lunch, prepared by our onboard chefs, we head to South Plaza Island.

Spot frigatebirds, Swallow-tailed Gulls and Galápagos Shearwaters gliding on the breeze. Here, among a dazzling array of flora, land iguanas laze by the shore while marine iguanas slip in and out of the water.

itinerary.heading: Explore Santa Cruz
itinerary.body:
Learn about local conservation on Santa Cruz Island

Today you'll visit the Charles Darwin Research Station in Puerto Ayora, where a team of 200 work to conserve the local wildlife. Here you can see baby tortoises and Darwin’s famous finches - the birds he used as a basis for his theory of evolution.

Experience a cooler climate over lunch in the lush highlands, where giant tortoises roam, munching on grass and wallowing in pools.

Then there's time for an optional activity, including mountain biking or kayaking in beautiful Tortuga Bay. Or hike to the snow-white beach of Playa Brava and the secluded mangrove cove at Playa Mansa.

itinerary.heading: Dramatic Española
itinerary.body:
Lava lizards and incredible birdlife

Your Galápagos cruise reaches Española, the archipelago's most southerly island. Birdlife here is truly extraordinary - look out for Waved Albatrosses, Nazca Boobies, Blue-footed Boobies and Swallow-tailed Gulls.

It’s also a chance to spot red Española lava lizards and marine iguanas, as well as see the famous blowhole, El Soplador, blasting water 75 ft into the air.

After lunch on board the ship, we'll head to the picturesque coral beach of Gardner Bay and nearby Osborn Islet, to seek out sea lions, mockingbirds and finches. If you're feeling active, you can go snorkelling or join an optional kayaking excursion.

itinerary.heading: Reef life on Eden Islet
itinerary.body:
Green turtles, sharks and rare bird colonies

The wealth of wildlife-watching opportunities continues at Eden Islet, where we hope to see Galápagos green turtles, rays and friendly reef sharks. On the shore, look out for distinctive frigatebirds with their rubbery, red throats.

You can swim or snorkel to explore the reefs. Or you may also have a chance to see the reefs from our glass-bottomed boat or by kayak. After lunch, we'll sail to North Seymour.

The island is a great site for spotting colonies of Blue-footed Boobies and Swallow-tailed Gulls. Sea lions and marine iguanas also congregate here, attracted by the bountiful sea life in its waters.

itinerary.heading: Back to Baltra Island
itinerary.body:
The end of an incredible wildlife adventure

Your expedition cruise around the Galápagos Islands draws to a close as you disembark at Baltra Island. From here, you'll fly to Guayaquil, where a friendly representative will help you connect to your international flight. From here it's on to Quito.

As you leave this fascinating region, you'll take with you incredible memories of amazing wildlife and wonderful experiences in this unique part of the world that few have the privilege of seeing.

Back in the charming city of Quito, you'll have time to explore and see some of the sights you may have missed at the start of your trip.

itinerary.heading: Heading home
itinerary.body:
Say goodbye to South America

Enjoy a delicious breakfast at your hotel, before preparing for your journey home.

We hope you are left with some amazing memories of the incredible scenery and wildlife of the Galápagos and Ecuador, as well as thoughts of your newfound friends and the wonderful adventure you experienced together.

itinerary.heading: Adventures in Anchorage
itinerary.body:
Experience the sights and sounds of Alaska’s capital

Anchorage is packed with places to explore and enjoy, from restaurants and galleries to sports venues and shops. If you can, it's worth extending your time here. Anchorage Museum and the Native Heritage Center give you a taste of local culture. If you enjoy the outdoors, why not visit the flowering Town Square Park or go salmon fishing in Ship Creek. Animal lovers will love our optional Pre-Programme, which takes in the incredible Denali National Park. It's home to North America’s highest peak, and a first taste of the Alaskan wildlife you'll experience on your adventures.

itinerary.heading: Scenic road trip to Seward
itinerary.body:
Wild landscapes, ice fields and animal conservation

Our ride to Seward takes us through the Kenai Peninsula and some of the world’s most awe-inspiring back country scenery. Look out for the impressively-horned Dall sheep grazing on misty mountain slopes. On the way, we’ll stop at the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center to learn about their work rehabilitating orphaned or injured animals, from bears, bison and moose to eagles and owls. Our embarkation point, Seward, is the gateway to the vast, mountainous Kenai Fjords National Park, home to the largest ice fields in Alaska. A spectacular and fitting launch point for the adventures ahead.

itinerary.heading: Ivy League glaciers
itinerary.body:
Elemental nature and whimsical names

Your lecture today may well be related to glaciology. We visit College Fjord, which holds five tidewater glaciers, five valley glaciers and a dozen others. The 1899 Harriman Expedition team, which charted the fjord, named the glaciers after their alma maters, which include Vassar, Harvard and Yale. Princeton is missing, apparently a deliberate snub. We’ll get as close to the glaciers as we can, taking our small expedition boats on the fjord if possible, or in kayaks as an optional excursion. From the water, you might glimpse humpback whales, Bald Eagles, otters and sea lions that inhabit this icy wilderness.

itinerary.heading: Edge of the Copper River
itinerary.body:
Cordova's successful environmental recovery

Sitting in the Chugach National Forest and only accessible by boat or plane, remote Cordova has retained its tradition small-town authenticity, and its friendly residents will welcome you as you explore the salmon fishing town. You'll be in awe of its spectacular setting between Orca Inlet, Hawkins Island, Mount Eccles, Eyak Lake and the Copper River Delta.

In 1989, Cordova was probably best known for the Exxon Valdez oil spill. Today, after major clean up efforts, its coastline has mostly recovered, and you'll be able to see wildlife like sea otters, eagles, tundra swans, beavers, moose and bears.

itinerary.heading: Tidal Glaciers
itinerary.body:
Wildlife watching in glacier-fed waters

You'll experience an amazing expedition day in Icy Bay today. Three glaciers – Guyot, Yahtse and Tyndall – regularly calf into the bay. If conditions allow, the Expedition Team will take you ashore on the 34-mile-long, 8-mile-wide Guyot Glacier or you can explore in kayaks on an optional excursion.

Wildlife abounds in the Gulf of Alaska, offering unrivalled photography opportunities. Humpback whales, orcas, Stellar sea lions, sea otters and harbour seals lazing on floating chunks of ice, can be seen in these waters. Our onboard photographer is ready with expert tips on how to get the best from your camera.

itinerary.heading: William Henry Bay
itinerary.body:
Whale watching and wilderness exploration

In the afternoon, we’ll pass Point Adolphus on the northern tip of Chichagof Island, across from Glacier Bay National Park. These nutrient-rich waters are famous for attracting humpback whales and other marine life, so be sure to get out on deck and have your camera ready.

We'll visit William Henry Bay on our included excursion. Lying south of Haines, at the edge of the Chilkat mountain range, it's home to brown bears, black bears and moose. We’ll drop anchor here and explore the shores lined with old-growth forest under the guidance of an expert local guide.

itinerary.heading: Native art in Haines
itinerary.body:
Artist community in the 'Valley of the Eagles'

Haines was originally home to the Chilkat Tlingit people, renowned for their weaving skills. You’ll see examples of their intricate, beautiful work in the blankets on display in Haines Sheldon Museum. We’ll visit Fort Seward on an included excursion while we’re ashore, as well as the flourishing art scene in Haines itself. The galleries and workshops are filled with Totem carvings, silverwork and sculpture. Discover your own artistic side – try your photography skills on the incredible landscapes and wildlife. Look out for bears, moose, and the Bald Eagles for which this town is famous.

itinerary.heading: Holkham Bay fjords
itinerary.body:
Icebergs and wildlife in idyllic twin fjords

Holkham Bay has two arms – Tracy and Endicott – beautiful fjords that are out of reach for larger cruise ships. Your captain will decide which offers better exploration options on the day, but don't worry, both are equally special.

At the end of each fjord, fresh icebergs calve from the glaciers against a stunning backdrop of forested cliffs. Endicott Arm is a breeding ground for harbour seals, often seen on the floating ice. You might also see whales, bears, mountain goats and moose.

Get wildlife tips from our onboard photographer before we head out on expedition boats to get closer to these unique sights.

itinerary.heading: Sitka's blend of cultures
itinerary.body:
Stunning scenery and a unique mix of cultures

Surrounded by Tongass National Forest, Sitka is only accessible by sea and air. Get out on deck for stunning views of the Sisters Mountains and Mount Edgecumbe Volcano.

Discover Sitka's fascinating history with our Expedition Team. Inhabited by the Tlingit for 10,000 years, it was occupied by Russia in 1804, before being sold to America after the Crimean War. Today, Sitka blends all three cultures.

Visit the Russian Orthodox cathedral and Russian Bishop's House. Sitka National Historic Park is a real highlight, where you'll see ornate Haida and Tlingit totem poles. Or enjoy a walking trail through the forest to the ocean.

itinerary.heading: Alaska's 'Little Norway'
itinerary.body:
Humpback whales and the Devil's Thumb

We continue to cruise north to Petersburg, perched at the edge of stunning Frederick Sound. Settled by a Norwegian in the 1800s – and fondly known as 'Little Norway' – its shallow, bustling harbour houses Alaska's largest home-based halibut fishing fleet. Our ships are small enough to enter, and our shared Norwegian heritage makes for a great talking point with the local community as we explore this charming town. Don't miss the views from the waterfront. You can watch icebergs float down the sound, look across to North America’s biggest rockface, the Devil’s Thumb, and in summer, the waters attract feeding humpback whales.

itinerary.heading: Wrangell's Petroglyphs
itinerary.body:
Visit one of Alaska’s oldest harbour towns

Our cruise of the Alaskan islands takes us to Wrangell. A mile out of town you’ll find the ancient rock carvings of Petroglyph Beach. Bring paper and take some stone rubbings as a unique souvenir. Learn more about Wrangell's fascinating past in the local museum. Now part of the US, it’s been governed by Britain, Russia and the Tlingit people. On Shakes Island, the Chief Shakes Tribal House and totem poles tell the Tlingit story. Your visit includes a trip on the waters in our small expedition boats. On land, hikers will enjoy the nature trails from Stikine River and Mount Dewey to the rainforest.

itinerary.heading: Beautiful Misty Fjords
itinerary.body:
Alaskan wilderness where wildlife thrives all around

Part of the Tongass National Forest, Misty Fjords is a pristine wilderness of evergreens, waterfalls and snow-capped peaks. Influential mountaineer John Muir described it as one of the most beautiful places he’d ever seen. Weather permitting, you'll join the Expedition Team to tour Misty Fjords on small expedition boats or take kayaks out for an optional excursion.

Look out for mountain goats, bears and moose. In the water, you'll find Pacific salmon, along with otters, sea lions, harbour seals, orcas and Dall porpoises. And look skywards for hummingbirds, herons and Bald Eagles.

itinerary.heading: Canada's Inside Passage
itinerary.body:
Up close to nature as we explore islands and channels

On our smaller expedition ships, you'll get an unrivalled intimate experience of the protected North American Pacific Fjordland. As we navigate the lesser-travelled channels, you’ll get close to the beautiful and fascinating scenery. Keep your binoculars close at hand. As always, there’s plenty to see and learn in the Science Center, with insightful lectures from your Expedition Team, and opportunities to swap memories of your adventures. This is also a great time to wind down, with a little pampering in the spa or sitting up on deck with your fellow explorers as the stunning scenery slips by.

itinerary.heading: First Nations encounter
itinerary.body:
Indigenous heritage and rich wildlife in Alert Bay

We arrive in Alert Bay, a scenic village on Cormorant Island, north of Vancouver Island. Here we'll have the opportunity to meet and learn from the Kwakwaka’wakw First Nations community – to be welcomed by them is a real privilege. We’ll experience more at the U'mista Cultural Centre, where you'll see elaborate totem poles, paintings, carvings and ceremonial masks. You'll also see a dance performance. The island’s sheltered waters attract a huge array of wildlife – the Yellow-billed Loon, with its distinctive speckled back, is a particular highlight. We might even see orcas and humpback whales close to shore.

itinerary.heading: Vibrant Vancouver
itinerary.body:
Enjoy British Columbia’s largest city

Our expedition cruise ends in the beautiful city of Vancouver at the foot of the Rockies. Visit Gastown, the city's oldest neighbourhood, and climb Vancouver Lookout for a citywide panorama overlooking neon-lit Granville Street, West End beaches and the towering cedars of Stanley Park. 

Vancouver has a flavour all its own – and so does its global cuisine. Dine out in Chinatown, Punjabi Market or Little Italy as you soak up the city's buzzing atmosphere.

While you're here, you might want to join our Post-Programme to the beautiful mountain resort of Whistler. What better way to end your adventure.

itinerary.heading: Setting off from Hamburg
itinerary.body:
Your Atlantic coast adventure starts here

Our expedition cruise begins in Hamburg, the 'Venice of the North', where you'll board our stylish, hybrid-powered expedition ship, MS Fridtjof Nansen. But with so much to see and do in Hamburg, why not spend some time here first and book our optional Pre-Programme city tour.

You'll discover most of the city's attractions in the Altstadt, including St Nikolai Memorial and Deichstraße Historic Street, and you can also explore two UNESCO World Heritage Sites – Chilehaus and the world's largest warehouse complex. Or enjoy a boat tour of the city's canals and harbour front.

itinerary.heading: Potter around Harlingen
itinerary.body:
Experience the Frisian port city of Harlingen

You can walk or bike around Harlingen – a city of canals, pretty harbours and home to the last traditional pottery factory in the Netherlands. It lies on the shores of the Wadden Sea, a UNESCO World Heritage area.

In the Old Town, look out for the 46 Stumbling Stones, memorialising 46 Jewish residents murdered during the Nazi occupation.

You'll find traditional sailing ships and historic warehouses around the old harbours of Noorderhaven and Zuiderhaven. And stop at the Harlingen Aardewerk Museum for examples of distinctive Frisian pottery.

itinerary.heading: Cruising the channel
itinerary.body:
Learn, relax and dine on board

Enjoy the day on board relaxing on deck, in the Explorer Lounge or in the Science Center, as we cruise towards France. 

While the British call these waters the English Channel, it’s more commonly known on the continent as La Manche, or derivations of that. The Dutch may have the most diplomatic name for it… they simply call it Het Kanaal - the Channel. 

Take in the sea views from the pool or hot tubs, and then dine on delicious, locally sourced food from one of the three onboard restaurants.

itinerary.heading: Normandy past and present
itinerary.body:
Discover historic beaches, Caen and WWII memorials 

Normandy's history goes far back. While the region is well known for the 1944 D-Day landings, these beaches were once invaded by Vikings. You'll discover more on today's included excursion. Learn about WWII history in Ouistreham’s Musée de Debarquement No 4 Commando, the German fortifications at the Grand Bunker Mur de l’Atlantique Musée, and the war cemetery at Hermanville-sur-Mer. Your other included excursion today will be to pretty Caen, where you'll explore the 12th century St Samson church and the 11th century Saint-Étienne Romanesque church. Other highlights include the Mémorial de Caen Museum and the Musée des Beaux-Arts.

itinerary.heading: The Citadel of Saint-Malo
itinerary.body:
A beautiful Breton town steeped in history

Viewed from the sea, Saint-Malo is an impressive sight, fringed by fortified bastions and shallow beaches. A circular walk along the ramparts offers the best views of the town and surrounding islands. Take a tour of the Privateers house to learn about the ruthless Corsairs and the town’s pirate heritage.

You can also follow the historical trail within the old city walls through a maze of cobbled streets. The Gothic-style St Vincent Cathedral and the Chateau de la Duchesse Anne are worth a visit. And at low tide, you can walk to the fortified island, Le Grand-Bé, where famous local writer Chateaubriand is buried.

itinerary.heading: Land's End at Finistère
itinerary.body:
Inspiring coastal scenery and maritime history

Finistère, the 'Land's End' of France, is a picturesque region of colourful quaysides, beautiful beaches and craggy cliff faces. We’ll visit one of two ports today – Douarnenez or Brest – depending on conditions, but will enjoy the same exciting excursion programme. The coastal landscape around Douarnenez inspired both Renoir and Boudin, and will take your breath away. Its fishermen’s huts and seaman chapels are romantic reminders of its fishing heritage. Your included expedition will take you on a guided coastal walk to the Pointe du Raz. Alternatively, we'll explore the lively quays and docks of Brest, a fascinating maritime city. Visit the National Naval Museum or enjoy a cable car ride with breathtaking views of Brest and the Recouvrance Bridge.

itinerary.heading: Morbihan's wild beauty
itinerary.body:
Experience Brittany's wild coastline

Immerse yourself in Breton culture as we spend the day exploring the region of Morbihan. It's home to Brittany's finest natural scenery and sights, like the craggy cliffs of the Côte Sauvage, the medieval city of Vannes, and the Carnac Stones that rival Stonehenge.

We may anchor on Quiberon Bay, from where you can join optional excursions to historic sites. If we anchor at Belle Île, you’ll discover its formidable 17th century fortress Citadelle Vauban, in the charming port of Le Palais. Visit Les Aiguilles de Port Coton – famously painted by Claude Monet, take a coastal walk, or relax on Donnant beach.

itinerary.heading: Ile d’Aix, Emperor's Isle
itinerary.body:
A tiny island with a grand military history

It's hard to believe that this pretty little island has played a role in all the wars France has fought in, from the Middle Ages to the Second World War. Today, you can peacefully explore Ile d’Aix, with its quaint and colourful houses, by foot or by bike.

Your visit will reveal a Vauban-style fort village, lighthouses, fortresses, and the Napoleonic Museum, detailing the Emperor’s stay on the island, before he was exiled.

If it's tranquillity you're after, head to the island’s five white sand beaches. The island is also a birder's paradise, with over 200 species to spot.

itinerary.heading: Bordeaux, City of Wine
itinerary.body:
Raise a glass in Bordeaux, the City of Wine

Bordeaux's old town is a UNESCO World Heritage site, bursting with culture and craft at every turn. From the famous water mirror at Place de la Bourse, to the French Gothic Cathedral de St André and the Musée des Beaux-Arts, if you love art and architecture, you're spoilt for choice.

But it's wine that's the true soul of Bordeaux. With over 8,500 chateaux and producers in the region, and vineyards just a short tram ride from town, you can taste and compare some of the 60 appellations, from the stellar Red Bordeaux Supérieur to sweet Sauternes.

itinerary.heading: Explore San Sebastián
itinerary.body:
Experience the jewel of the Basque country

We leave France behind as our expedition cruise continues to Spain. You'll love the energy of San Sebastián – which offers something for everyone – food lovers, culture buffs and surfers.

Visit the historic district of Parte Vieja with its Gothic church, Baroque facades and beautiful squares. You can relax on La Concha beach or take a cable car to Monte Igueldo; while the steep ascent up Monte Urgull will reward you with fantastic bay views from its fortifications.

Make sure you find time to sample some traditional Basque cuisine. The delicious pintxos are perfect small bites to devour as you tour the city.

itinerary.heading: Golden Sands of Gijón
itinerary.body:
Savour a different cultural flavour in Asturias

Enjoying a prime position along the Bay of Biscay, Gijón, the cultural heart of Asturias, has grown from a small fishing village settled by the Romans into a prominent port city.

You can experience its old town charm on a stroll through the Cimadevilla and Barrio del Carmen districts, exploring beautiful Baroque churches and the Plaza del Marques of the Old Quarter. Or climb the hilly peninsula of Cimadevilla, Gijón’s historic centre.

Then relax on the golden sands of Playa de San Lorenzo, enjoy a coastal walk, or savour freshly caught fish and other Asturian delicacies, accompanied by a glass of refreshing local cider.

itinerary.heading: Galician Coast
itinerary.body:
Ferrol's naval history is a must for maritime aficionados

Ferrol is one of the best-preserved examples of an 18th century port city. Explore the maritime museums, and stroll through Barrio de la Magdalena, with its unusual Neoclassical 'chessboard' street grid design.

Or venture northwest to Costa de Artabra, with its spectacular coastal landscapes. You can sample Galician specialities like pulpo á feira, octopus with potatoes and paprika, in eateries along the local beaches.

Camino Ingles, one of the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage routes, starts in Ferrol. Join an optional excursion direct to Santiago de Compostela, one the most important Catholic sites in the world.

itinerary.heading: Charismatic Porto
itinerary.body:
Explore the UNESCO-listed historic centre of Porto

Arriving in Portugal, we dock at Leixoes. From here, you can see the Lighthouse of Leça, the Chapel of Boa Nova and the beautiful Praia Azul beach. 

Included today is a walking tour of nearby Porto – famed for its port wine and UNESCO-listed historic centre. Its undulating streets are made for strolling, with pastel houses, colourful tiled facades, street art, ornate churches and panoramic views across the Douro.

Stroll along the bustling Ribeira Docks promenade, cross the Dom Luís I bridge, snack on delicious petiscos and enjoy wine tastings at the port cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia.

itinerary.heading: Enchanting Lisbon
itinerary.body:
One of southern Europe's most captivating cities

Our expedition cruise ends in Lisbon. The Portuguese capital is rich in history and culture. If you have time, it's definitely worth exploring.

Lisbon's districts each have their own distinctive essence. Explore lively Baixa and elegant Chiado. Then head to the more traditional Alfama, where you'll find the Moorish fortress, São Jorge Castle. For a more bohemian view of Lisbon, head down the narrow streets of Bairro Alto.

You can also visit the beautiful UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Torre de Belém and Mosteiro dos Jerónimos a little further out from the city centre, where you'll also find the delicious pastéis de Belém.

itinerary.heading: Maritime Portsmouth
itinerary.body:
Centuries of seafaring traditions in this historic city

Our expedition begins in Portsmouth, a modern coastal city with a fascinating naval heritage. If you have time, it's worth spending a few hours wandering its cobbled streets and visiting historic attractions like the HMS Victory and the Mary Rose.

In the port, your hybrid-powered ship, MS Fridtjof Nansen, awaits. Once you’ve collected your complimentary expedition jacket and settled in, you’ll meet your Expedition Team.

As we set sail for Fowey, you can explore the ship, take in the views from deck, and enjoy delicious, local produce in one of our excellent onboard restaurants. Your British Isles adventure has begun.

itinerary.heading: The Cornish Riviera
itinerary.body:
Romantic landscapes, Cornish teas and conservation

Home to Arthurian legends, pirates of old and one of the UK’s most beautiful coastlines – it can only be Cornwall.

We’ll anchor outside Fowey – pronounced ‘Foy’ – a picturesque harbour town in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Then head ashore to explore its quaint streets, and maybe try a clotted cream ice, some local ale or a traditional Cornish pasty.

Hiking possibilities include local beauty spots like Gribbin Head, Pont Pill Creek and Readymoney Cove. You can also visit the Eden Project, an eco education and research centre like no other, with an immense ‘captive’ rainforest, and inspiring installations.

itinerary.heading: Vikings of Waterford
itinerary.body:
Norse heritage in a beautiful Irish city by the sea

The Emerald Isle is the next stop on your expedition cruise. We'll visit Ireland’s oldest city – Waterford. Famous for its fine crystal, a trip to the House of Waterford Crystal Visitor Centre is a must.

Take time to explore Waterford's Viking Triangle district, and its fascinating museums, including the King of the Vikings Museum, where virtual reality takes you back to the 10th century.

Nearby, you can visit Kilkenny Castle, built by the Normans, or cycle along the Waterford Greenway. Or perhaps visit the Copper Coast UNESCO Geopark, with its stunning scenery, captivating ruins and ancient dolmen.

itinerary.heading: Arrival in Liverpool
itinerary.body:
Discover Liverpool's maritime and musical legacy

Your historic ports' cruise would not be complete without a visit to Liverpool – a key trade and migration port for over 300 years. We end our expedition in this lively city.

Head to the Mersey waterfront to find the iconic mercantile buildings known as the ‘Three Graces' – the Royal Liver Building, Cunard Building and Port of Liverpool Building.

The city is also famously the home of The Beatles, and music lovers can join a tour of their favourite haunts, like Penny Lane, Strawberry Fields and The Cavern Club. Then relax at the Royal Albert Dock as you reflect on your maritime adventures.

heading: Expedition Cruise to the White Sea – Norway and Russia Adventure
intro: Explore Norway’s coast as we cross the Arctic Circle, before venturing east to Russia’s White Sea. Join us for an exhilarating cruise visiting settlements rich in fishing traditions and Sámi history, as well as the iconic Solovetsky Islands. We’ll hope to see spectacular autumn hues, snow-topped mountains and – just maybe – the magical glow of the Northern Lights.

itinerary.heading: Set sail from Bergen
itinerary.body:
Visit UNESCO-listed Bryggen and Mount Fløyen

Your expedition cruise begins in beautiful Bergen. Surrounded by mountains and the sea, the old capital is one of Norway’s most picturesque cities. Join our Pre-Programme for a guided tour of the sights, including the famous Bryggen district, with its colourful wooden wharfs. If you have time, take the funicular railway up to the summit of Mount Fløyen for amazing views over the city. Then it's time to board MS Spitsbergen, the ideal ship to navigate the Norwegian coastline and Russia's White Sea up close.

Settle in to your cabin, meet your expert Expedition Team, and enjoy your first dinner aboard as we sail towards Hjørundfjorden.

itinerary.heading: Stunning Hjørundfjorden
itinerary.body:
Lofty peaks, still waters and traditional farms lie off the tourist track

The Norwegian fjords are famed for their breathtaking beauty. Even so, Hjørundfjorden will amaze you. This natural wonder, far from the well-trodden tourist track, is one of the purest and most beautiful fjords in Norway Still waters are surrounded by the majestic Sunnmore Alps. A few tiny farms dot the shoreline – your Expedition Team will explain the traditional methods that the farmers use to work this tricky terrain, handed down for generations. We’ll anchor close to one of the settlements and head ashore to explore the scenic landscape in the crisp autumn air.

itinerary.heading: Sailing north
itinerary.body:
Time to fully explore your ship and prepare for the Northern Lights

As your cruise heads to the picture-perfect Lofoten Islands, you’ll have time to see all MS Spitsbergen has to offer.

Work out in the gym or be pampered in the Wellness Spa. Soak in one of the hot tubs, or relax in the panoramic sauna and watch the landscapes slip by. Over the next few days, we may see the Northern Lights. Your Expedition Team will give you tips for capturing the colours on camera, as well as delivering informative, interactive sessions in the Explorer Lounge. These are a great way to bring your destinations to life, with a mix of fascinating facts and marvellous myths.

itinerary.heading: The Lofoten Islands
itinerary.body:
Pretty villages nestle among untamed mountain peaks

The starkly beautiful Lofoten islands – with a rich Viking heritage – combine dramatic peaks, sheltered coves, sandy beaches and pristine waters.

The winter fishing season has been a way of life here for centuries, when Arctic cod come here to spawn. You’ll see fishing villages, with their cabins – or rorbu – set out in rows along the shore. You might even spot the fishermen's wooden racks air-drying cod.

Svolvær, the biggest town on the archipelago, is close to Lofoten’s many magnificent sights. Here you can enjoy activities such as kayaking, hiking and expedition boating, or simply a wander round the shops, galleries and cafés.

itinerary.heading: Picture-perfect Sommarøy
itinerary.body:
Embrace this welcoming island community and its outdoor pursuits

Nestled amid astonishingly blue waters and majestic mountain scenery, Sommarøy is a small village with plenty to see and do.

One of the best ways to experience local life is to visit the village shop. Here you’ll find the Kaillkråa, a cosy corner where friends catch up. You’ll be warmly welcomed if you’d like to pull up a chair and join the conversation.

You can also choose one of our optional excursions, hiking in the peaceful hills or kayaking in the crystal island waters. Or visit nearby Tromsø – the ‘Gateway to the Arctic’ – which we'll also return to later as our final stop on your cruise.

itinerary.heading: The North Cape
itinerary.body:
Visit the North Cape – at the top of the world

From the fishing village of Skarsvåg, you'll enjoy an included excursion to the mountain plateau of the North Cape.

At just 1,300 miles from the Geographic North Pole, it's one of the northernmost points in Europe. Enjoy cliff-edge views out to sea, take a selfie at the Globe Monument, then visit the cinema to see a short film about the plateau and exhibits about the island’s history. You can also an optional walk with the Expedition Team to Kirkeporten viewpoint, a natural arch in the rock. You’ll want a scenic snap of the extraordinary hornet, a formation remarkably like an animal horn.

itinerary.heading: Trading history of Vardø
itinerary.body:
Step back in time in Norway’s easternmost settlement

Our final stop in Norway is Vardø. This was an important trading centre for Russia’s Pomor people and those of northern Norway. The fascinating economic and cultural connections are explained in the Pomor Museum. The darker side of the town’s history is commemorated by the extraordinary witch monument, a memorial to the 91 people tried and executed for witchcraft in the 17th century. A visit to the museum at Vardøhus Fortress, where the accused were held, is recommended. If you’d like to explore the wider area more, your Expedition Team will lead you on a nature walk.

itinerary.heading: Welcome to Russia
itinerary.body:
Exploring the maritime and military history of Murmansk

The Russian leg of our expedition begins in the largest city north of the Arctic Circle: Murmansk. Its streets hold many monuments celebrating its history and achievements. You’ll see the first before we land. A 115ft Russian WW2 soldier stands at the port, memorialising those who gave their lives. Elsewhere Lenin, the world’s first nuclear icebreaker, is an interactive museum telling the history of the icebreaker fleet. From here on, the ever-changing conditions will make your cruise unique. Our Expedition Team will adapt each day to create the most memorable itinerary for you.

itinerary.heading: Journey to the White Sea
itinerary.body:
Preparing for the unspoilt marvels ahead with your Expedition Team

Sailing into the White Sea was forbidden for many years. Together with its geographically remote location, that means its rich history and incredible natural beauty remain a mystery to many.

There’s a great deal to discover as we head for Arkhangelsk. Our journey follows Pomor trade routes around the coastline of the Barents Sea.

On the way your Expedition Team and their Russian colleagues will tell you about the destinations ahead. They’ll discuss subjects such as life in the far north of Russia, the area’s trading histor,y and the fascinating cultures of the Sámi and Pomor peoples.

itinerary.heading: Russia’s cultural capital
itinerary.body:
A stunning seaport with centuries of history to explore

Arkhangelsk was the chief port of medieval and early modern Russia, and has been an important seaport, trading, and shipbuilding centre for centuries. Key industries are fishing and timber – this last you can see from the architecture. The beautifully-preserved buildings of Malye Korely open-air museum showcase the incredible talent of artisans down the ages. Arkhangelsk’s history incorporates everything from Soviet times to Peter the Great. There’s much to learn, so the Lore Museum in the Merchant Yard is worth a visit. Want a true taste of history? Try kozoola, traditional Pomor gingerbread.

itinerary.heading: Pearls of the White Sea
itinerary.body:
Discover the history and beauty of this UNESCO World Heritage Site

The Solovetsky Islands are sometimes called ‘the pearls of the White Sea’ – and it’s easy to see why. Their incredible history is surpassed only by their astonishing beauty. You’ll visit Solovetsky Monastery on Bolshoy Solovetsky, which grew into a huge medieval political power and became a massive fortified citadel. Standing against a hauntingly beautiful and stunningly remote background, it’s a sight you won’t ever forget Both the Monastery and the Solovetsky islands are UNESCO World Heritage sites, and a standing monument to the extraordinary history of this endlessly-fascinating country.

itinerary.heading: The Kola Peninsula
itinerary.body:
Natural harbours and scattered settlements where tradition is still strong

Autumn is a changeable time, so our itinerary for the Kola Peninsula will depend on tides and weather conditions. Today's goal is to reach Chapoma or Pyalitsa, traditional settlements of houses built from wood and natural materials.

People here still rely on traditional fishing and hunting methods used by original settlers. If we’re able to land, you’ll really appreciate the challenges that face those who call this area home. At the same time the wild remoteness of the landscape and views across the White Sea create a strangely delicate beauty that you’ll want to capture on camera.

itinerary.heading: Relax at sea
itinerary.body:
Sit back and reflect on your adventures so far

After an enjoyable few days exploring some of the secrets that the White Sea has to offer, you’ll welcome the chance to relax as we sail back towards the Norwegian border. Your Expedition Team will look back over your journey so far, answering any questions you may have and helping you fill in any gaps in what you’ve learned. They’ll also talk about what’s planned for the final leg of your expedition. This is also a great time to make the most of your onboard facilities, from the gym, sauna and hot tub to the Wellness Spa and Explorer Lounge.

itinerary.heading: Return to Murmansk
itinerary.body:
Another chance to experience the city's history and people

There’s so much to experience in Murmansk that you'll appreciate a second visit. You’ll have time to explore further and learn more about life in the largest city north of the Arctic Circle. Take time to visit the Lighthouse Memorial and Church of the Saviour on the Waters. Together they form a complex dedicated to the memory of Murmansk sailors, military and civilians who lost their lives at sea. You'll great a feel for this modern city and its people by popping into its many restaurants and bars. And don't forget to pick up a souvenir on your last day in Russia.

itinerary.heading: Troms og Finnmarken
itinerary.body:
Exploring the Barents Sea

Any true expedition is all about adapting to conditions and today is no exception. Our aim is to get as close as we can to the rugged Norwegian coastline.

Landscapes in the Barents Sea vary from barren coastal areas facing the sea, to more sheltered fjord areas and river valleys with gullies and trees.

We’ll explore the area of Troms og Finnmarken, seeking a suitable fjord, island or bay to anchor in. Then we’ll use small expedition boats to go ashore and see what discoveries we can make.

itinerary.heading: Awe-inspiring Lyngen Alps
itinerary.body:
Enjoy a taste of traditional life at the foot of the Lyngen Alps

This morning you'll arrive at a sparkling fjord at the base of the awe-inspiring Lyngen Alps and the charming coastal trading post of Havnnes. Characterised by old, white-painted houses peeking over the waterline, this tiny town sends you back to the days of steam and sail. Visit the warehouse where locals use centuries-old methods to cure stockfish or the vintage general store. The local museum features an exhibition about Annie Giæver, who photographed local life during the early 20th century. If the weather is kind to us, we’ll explore the spectacular surroundings by kayak or on foot.

itinerary.heading: Arriving at Tromsø
itinerary.body:
Tromsø is a town of many sights – that may include the Northern Lights

Your expedition cruise to the White Sea reaches journey's end in Tromsø. You can choose to extend your adventure with our optional Post-Programme – enjoy an extra night and a trip around the city, plus a ride on the Fjellheisen cable car. Even if you can’t extend your stay, it’s worth taking time to explore the city’s attractions. Those might include the Northern Lights, so keep your cameras handy. The cable car offers breathtaking views of the city and surrounding countryside. Or visit Ølhallen, the town’s oldest pub, for a beer from the world’s northernmost brewery, Mack.

itinerary.heading: Valparaíso, a UNESCO gem
itinerary.body:
Valparaíso truly is the 'Jewel of the Pacific'

Your expedition cruise begins in colourful Valparaíso, known as the 'Jewel of the Pacific'. Friendly and bursting with colour, this gloriously sprawling UNESCO-listed city is filled with exciting smells, sounds and people. It’s an exhilarating maze of hillside alleyways and barrios, winding streets of colourful houses and mercados packed with local produce. Take it all in on the funicular ride up to Cerro Alegre and Concepción. If you'd like to explore more of the region, you can join our optional Pre-Programme to tour the extraordinary Atacama Desert before you embark MS Fridtjof Nansen, your hybrid-powered expedition ship.

itinerary.heading: Orientation and discovery
itinerary.body:
Get into expedition mode

Over the next two days at sea, you'll learn more about the wonders we'll encounter during our trip.

Our Expedition team are experts in fields from oceanography and geology to ornithology and history. Get stuck in with fascinating lectures, hands-on presentations in the Science Center, and learn about our Citizen Science projects.

It's also the perfect time to unwind. With three excellent restaurants, a pool, hot tubs and wellness centre – not to mention our Explorer Lounge & Bar – you’ll have everything you need to relax, recharge, and get ready for adventure.

itinerary.heading: Castro's Chilotan charm
itinerary.body:
Stilt houses and historic churches

Set among the lush vegetation of Chiloé Island, Castro is Chile’s third oldest city and home to two UNESCO World Heritage Sites – Iglesia San Francisco and Iglesia de Señora de Gracia de Nercón.

You can enjoy terrific views of the city’s colourful palafitos – stilt houses along the waterfront – from the nearby hills, so keep your camera ready. For some culture, head to the Regional Museum and the Museum of Modern Art.

Bring your binoculars as Chiloé is an important habitat for bird species like Green-backed Firecrowns and Chilean flamingos. It’s also home to penguins, Black-necked swans, Ringed Kingfishers and Silvery Grebes.

itinerary.heading: The waters of Patagonia
itinerary.body:
Unforgettable Andean seascapes

We cruise south towards Puerto Natales, the capital of Última Esperanza. The iceberg-studded waters of Patagonia are captivating, with stunning shades of blue, from the brightest aquamarine to the deepest midnight hues.

As we sail, there's a good chance you’ll see whales, seabirds, penguins and more. Take in the scenery from the panoramic sauna or on-deck hot tubs and pool, enjoy locally sourced cuisine, or relax in the Explorer Lounge.

Our Expedition Team will be on hand with fascinating lectures on local history and wildlife, and our onboard photographer can help with tips on landscape photography.

itinerary.heading: Remote Puerto Edén
itinerary.body:
Discover Kawéskar culture in a Patagonian village

After cruising through Patagonian waters, we arrive at the enchanting village of Puerto Edén in Bernardo O’Higgins National Park.

This tiny village sits at the end of a deep fjord. It’s only accessible by sea, and the ferry that connects it to the mainland only visits once a month. There are no roads here – just wooden boardwalks connecting houses and shops.

Among its 250-strong population, you’ll meet some of the last remaining members of the indigenous Kawéskar, giving you a fascinating insight into Patagonian culture. The unique community is designated a Living Human Treasure by UNESCO.

itinerary.heading: Bohemian Puerto Natales
itinerary.body:
Gateway to Torres del Paine

Our expedition cruise continues to Puerto Natales, where we'll spend the night. You can opt to go hiking in Torres del Paine National Park – an incredible experience well worth doing.

The rugged landscape has steppe, forest and desert, punctuated by glaciers and lakes. Guanacos, rheas and pumas roam freely. Look out for Chilean Flamingos and you may even spot the mighty Andean condor.

Puerto Natales is a popular hub for hikers and adventurers, with many eateries, bars and outdoor shops. Visit the artisan village at Etherh Aike; enjoy a gin tour at the Last Hope Distillery; or stroll the photogenic waterfront.

itinerary.heading: Exploring Chile's fjords
itinerary.body:
Dramatic landscapes and incredible wildlife

We cruise south along the Chilean coast through the ruggedly beautiful, broken island chains of the fjords of Magallanes Province. Isolated islands and hidden bays create a rich haven for wildlife.

From deck, you can scan for colonies of Magellanic Penguins. If you’re lucky you might also spot elephant seals and whales. Or you can get hands on in the Science Center and study ice samples under the microscopes.

Your day’s activities will be decided by your Expedition Team. If the conditions are right, we'll take to the water in our small expedition boats for a closer look, or you might join a guided hike on a glacier.

itinerary.heading: Rounding Cape Horn
itinerary.body:
Learn how to protect Antarctic habitats

After sailing through the Beagle Channel, we’ll pass the southernmost tip of South America, Cape Horn. Once treacherous for sailors, today we'll round it in comfort. Conditions can still be changeable, but if weather allows, we'll even attempt to land there.

From here, we'll navigate the legendary Drake Passage towards Antarctica. En route, you'll find out what lies ahead and how to make your visit as safe and as sustainable as possible.

In the Science Center, the Expedition Team will give lectures about Antarctica’s animals, history, geology, as well as the impact of climate change and plastic pollution. You can also get involved in our Citizen Science projects.

itinerary.heading: Antarctica: another world
itinerary.body:
The most remote and starkly beautiful place on earth

Nothing prepares you for your first sight of Antarctica’s immense, frozen beauty. Icebergs, sculpted by nature, float in the straits. Gentoo and chinstrap penguins court while Adélie penguins nest. Over 45 species of seabird wheel overhead. Here, nature is king and we are mere observers.

You’ll spend an exciting four days busily exploring several of more than 20 possible landing sites, on and around the Antarctic Peninsula and South Shetland Islands. Wherever we go and whatever we do, each day will offer something different and thrilling. 

We might sail into a flooded volcanic caldera or land in icy bays, where remnants of whaling paraphernalia lie abandoned. You may also get a chance to go kayaking among icebergs and seals, or snowshoe to penguin colonies on optional activities.

Bird enthusiasts should look skywards for Antarctic seabirds such as skuas, jaegers, petrels and terns. Through Citizen Science projects and onboard lectures you'll learn more about polar exploration, this precious habitat, and how we can all protect it.

itinerary.heading: Sailing towards Argentina
itinerary.body:
Time to relax and relive your adventures

After four days expedition cruising in Antarctica, it’s time to head back. Recap your experiences with your Expedition Team and fellow guests, visit the Science Center, relax in the Explorer Lounge, or share a delicious meal as the waves roll by.

You'll be joined on board by an anthropologist and some younger members of the Yaghan community from Puerto Williams. Learn about the life and traditions, and the challenges they face in modern Chile, in a presentation, followed by some traditional songs.

Make the most of your time on board with some pampering in our Wellness Centre. Unwind in the sauna, pool and hot tubs too before we arrive in Ushuaia.

itinerary.heading: Ushuaia and Buenos Aires
itinerary.body:
Enjoy an expedition finale in Buenos Aires

Your expedition cruise ends in Ushuaia in Tierra del Fuego, Argentina’s southernmost province. From here, you’ll take a flight back to Buenos Aires, but it doesn’t have to be the end of your adventure.

Why not join our popular Post-Programme to tour the legendary Iguazu Falls, an amazing way to wrap up your travels. Or you can stay on in Buenos Aires, enjoying the city sights, cosmopolitan culture and tango shows before heading home.

itinerary.heading: Set sail from Hamburg
itinerary.body:
Your historic seaport adventure begins

Your expedition cruise sets sail from Hamburg – a city full of history, art and culture. There's plenty to see and do here. You can join our optional Pre-Programme before boarding MS Fridtjof Nansen.

Once you've collected your complimentary expedition jacket and settled into your cabin, take some time to explore the comforts on board your ship – designed for more sustainable exploration. You'll also get to meet your Expedition Team.

Enjoy the first of many delicious, locally-sourced meals, as we head out into the North Sea and towards the English Channel. Our first port of call is Portsmouth.

itinerary.heading: Make discoveries at sea
itinerary.body:
Get set for your British Isles adventure

As your expedition cruise travels from Hamburg to Portsmouth, it's the perfect opportunity to learn more about the seaports ahead with your expert Expedition Team.

Join them for lectures in the Science Center, sharing insights on subjects such as the Viking heritage of Waterford, the geology of the Fowey Estuary in Cornwall, and plenty more.

Your day at sea gives you plenty of time to relax too and your next-generation expedition ship allows you to do that in style. Head to the spa, sauna or infinity pool. And try the Nordic and international dishes at our three restaurants.

itinerary.heading: Naval Portsmouth
itinerary.body:
A city with a proud naval heritage

Your expedition reaches Portsmouth, a modern seafaring city with a fascinating naval heritage. Everything related to Britain’s long love affair with the waves is to be found here.

Visit Portsmouth Historic Dockyard to see Admiral Nelson’s HMS Victory, Henry VIII’s Mary Rose, and the iron-clad frigate HMS Warrior. Then learn about Portsmouth's role in WWII at the D-Day Museum in Southsea.

In contrast to the ancient castles, Cathedral and cobblestone streets of Old Portsmouth, you'll find the ultra modern Spinnaker Tower at Gunwharf Quays, a dramatic 170m concrete and steel landmark.

itinerary.heading: The Cornish Riviera
itinerary.body:
Romantic landscapes, Cornish teas and conservation

Home to Arthurian legends, pirates of old and one of the UK’s most beautiful coastlines – it can only be Cornwall.

We’ll anchor outside Fowey – pronounced ‘Foy’ – a picturesque harbour town in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Then head ashore to explore its quaint streets, and maybe try a clotted cream ice, some local ale or a traditional Cornish pasty.

Hiking possibilities include local beauty spots like Gribbin Head, Pont Pill Creek and Readymoney Cove. You can also visit the Eden Project, an eco education and research centre like no other, with an immense ‘captive’ rainforest, and inspiring installations.

itinerary.heading: Vikings of Waterford
itinerary.body:
Norse heritage in a beautiful Irish city by the sea

The next stop on your expedition cruise is the Emerald Isle, and Ireland’s oldest city – Waterford. Famous for its fine crystal, a trip to the House of Waterford Crystal Visitor Centre is a must.

Take time to explore Waterford's Viking Triangle district, and its fascinating museums, including the King of the Vikings Museum, where virtual reality takes you back to the 10th century.

Nearby, you can visit Kilkenny Castle, built by the Normans, or cycle along the Waterford Greenway. Or perhaps visit the Copper Coast UNESCO Geopark, with its stunning scenery, captivating ruins and ancient dolmen.

itinerary.heading: Arrival in Liverpool
itinerary.body:
Discover Liverpool's maritime and musical legacy

Your cruise of England's historic seaports would not be complete without a visit to Liverpool – a key trade and migration port for over 300 years.

Head to the Mersey waterfront to find the iconic mercantile buildings known as the ‘Three Graces' – the Royal Liver Building, Cunard Building and Port of Liverpool Building.

The city is also famously the home of The Beatles, and music lovers can join a tour of their favourite haunts like Penny Lane, Strawberry Fields and The Cavern Club. Then relax at the Royal Albert Dock as you reflect on your maritime adventures.
